text:
Who is that siren with such sorrowful voice,

with flesh so white, with braid so brown?

—It is a ray of moonlight bathing in the fountain,

it is a ray of moonlight…


Who, crying my name, crosses the dwelling?

Who calls me at night in such trembling tones?

—It is a breath of wind sobbing in the tower,

it is a breath of wind…


Tell me, who are you, archangel whose wings burn

in the divine fire of evening, and you rise

through the glory of ether?

—They are the clouds that pass;

look closely, they are the clouds…


Who spilled her necklaces in the water, my God?

They are rain of diamonds on blue velvet.

—It is heaven's image pulsing in the river,

it is heaven's image…


O Lord! Beauty is only, then, a mirage!

Nothing but You are certain: be my last Master.

Where to find You—in the ether, in the earth, in myself?

—A little dream will guide you through each abyss,

a little dream…

translation.title: Who Is That Siren with Such a Sorrowful Voice...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem’s question-and-answer structure, shifting each apparition into moonlight, wind, clouds, heaven, and dream.
